samples.summary: MemDocStore.batch() clears the redo stack up front even when the batch turns out to write nothing, so a no-op batch silently destroys redo history (Yorkie keeps it)
samples.evidence: `batch()` does `this.undoStack.push(before); this.redoStack = [];` before running `fn` (memory.ts:197-198). In the `wroteNothing` branch (memory.ts:209-212) it pops the undo checkpoint again — but the already-cleared `redoStack` is never restored. The interface contract added in store.ts says "A batch that writes nothing pushes nothing", and YorkieDocStore genuinely pushes nothing and clears nothing (Yorkie only clears redo when the change has operations). So the two implementations diverge: after `undo()`, any batch whose body happens to write nothing (e.g. `resetNamedStyle` for a style with no override and no stranded flags) leaves `canRedo()` false under MemDocStore and true under Yorkie, losing the user's redo stack. The new test `a batch that writes nothing costs no undo unit` only asserts `canUndo()`, so nothing pins the redo side.

samples.summary: MemDocStore.batch()'s "wrote nothing" comparison compares a normalized clone against the raw live document, so a batch that truly wrote nothing can still leave a dead undo checkpoint
samples.evidence: `const before = cloneDocument(this.doc)` (memory.ts:196) runs every top-level block's style through `normalizeBlockStyle` (memory.ts:13-25), which fills in every DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE key. The equality test then does `JSON.stringify(before) === JSON.stringify(this.doc)` (memory.ts:211) against the *un-normalized* live doc. Any block whose style landed in `this.doc` without normalization — e.g. via `insertBlock`/`insertBlockAfter`/`insertBlocksAfter`/`updateBlock`, which only `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(block))` (memory.ts:66-82) — makes the two strings differ even when the batch wrote nothing, so the checkpoint is kept and the user gets a Cmd+Z that visibly does nothing (exactly the symptom this change exists to remove). Structural JSON.stringify equality is also key-order sensitive, which compounds the same risk.

samples.summary: The new "setDocument() must not be called inside batch()" rule is enforced only in YorkieDocStore; MemDocStore silently allows it and the DocStore.batch() contract does not mention it
samples.evidence: YorkieDocStore.setDocument throws when `this.activeRoot` is set (yorkie-doc-store.ts:796-798), but `MemDocStore.setDocument` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:47-49) has no such guard and the `batch()` contract in packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:50-77 lists four rules, none of which is this one. Consequence: code (tests, the visual/hunt harness at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:503 and harness/visual/docs-scenarios.tsx:108, packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:435) developed against MemDocStore can call `setDocument` inside a batch, get an undo checkpoint whose reversal wipes the freshly loaded document, and only discover the divergence as a runtime throw under the collaborative store. A guard whose rule is neither documented on the interface nor mirrored in the other implementation is a broken invariant across implementations.
searchedFor: grep 'implements DocStore' across packages (only memory.ts and yorkie-doc-store.ts)
read of DocStore.batch() jsdoc in packages/docs/src/store/store.ts

samples.summary: Several read paths still call `this.doc.getRoot()` while the batch's `doc.update` is open; correctness of the whole batch rests on an unverified SDK assumption and no test exercises it
samples.evidence: `withUpdate` routes writes to the ambient root, but reads do not: `getDocument()` falls through to `this.doc.getRoot()` whenever `dirty` is true (line 611-635), and `readDocStyles()` (645), `getPageSetup()` (685), `setHeader`/`setFooter` (710/749) and `anchorDocPosition()` (953) call it unconditionally. Inside a top-level `batch()` these all execute while the batch's single `doc.update` is still open — e.g. `writeStylesAndRematerialize` calls `this.getDocument()` (line 2787) from inside the batch, and `updateCursorPos` still runs `anchorDocPosition` mid-batch (line 3147-3150) mixing a raw `getRoot()` tree read with cache-derived block paths. The only justification is the prose at line 2835-2838 ("Reads … are safe inside an open update"); if `getRoot()` instead returns pre-update state (or the SDK refuses it), tree indices and cached document would disagree, producing wrong tree paths / caret anchors. Every new batch test seeds the cache with `setDocument()` first, so the `dirty === true` entry into a batch (the normal state right after a remote change) is never exercised.

samples.summary: On a throw inside the batch, `withNamedStyleChange` leaves the docs model cache holding writes Yorkie rolled back, and skips the repaint
samples.evidence: `withNamedStyleChange` (editor.ts:1080-1092) has no try/finally: if `write()` or `doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll()` throws, `invalidateLayout()`/`render()` never run and the exception propagates. YorkieDocStore.batch marks its own cache dirty on that path (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2885-2888), but `Doc._document` was refreshed by `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:516,532) from a store state Yorkie has since discarded, so the editor's model keeps blocks/styles that never landed in the CRDT and subsequent edits are computed against them.

samples.summary: `setCursorForHistory` called inside a batch now stages `pendingCursorPos` while its presence publish is dropped; if no write in the batch consumes it, the next unrelated write records a stale post-edit caret
samples.evidence: `setCursorForHistory` sets `this.pendingCursorPos = pos` and then calls `updateCursorPos` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3026-3027), which now returns early inside a batch (line 3153). If the batch makes no write that reaches `consumePendingCursor()` (line 3111), the stale pending cursor survives the batch and is consumed by the *next* store write, which records it via `recordHistoryPresence` as that write's post-edit caret — so undo/redo restores a caret from a different action. The new skip makes this window silent (no presence publish to mask it).
